role: Winter service duty officer at a county highways depot, reviewing each completed gritting run log before sign-off
setting: After every precautionary or reactive salting run, the vehicle's run log arrives at the duty desk. It combines the planned route, the latest road-surface forecast, telematics from the spreader, the salt loading and return figures, and short notes from the driver and depot. The duty officer checks one log at a time. They decide whether the log can be signed off, how much priority road was left deficient, how soon any gap will freeze, and what follow-up to order before conditions deteriorate.

treated_before_freeze.instructions: Every priority section was treated before its forecast freeze time.

criteria.true: All priority sections logged treated before freeze.
criteria.false: A priority section untreated, or treated after freeze.

salt_reconciles.instructions: Salt used matches approved spread rate across treated area, within 10%.

criteria.true: Net tonnage within 10% of expected usage.
criteria.false: Gap over 10%, or a tonnage figure unconfirmed.

follow_up.instructions: What follow-up should be ordered on this gritting run?

criteria.sign_off: Log accepted as complete; no further action required.
criteria.sign_off_noted: Accepted, with a minor discrepancy recorded for depot correction.
criteria.hold: Sign-off withheld until one missing confirmation is received.
criteria.partial_retreat: Named missed priority sections re-treated only; rest accepted.
criteria.full_rerun: Whole route re-treated because log cannot support coverage.

deficient_length.instructions: How much priority road was missed or treated below approved rate?
criteria: None: no priority road missed or undertreated
Minor: under 2 km of priority road affected
Moderate: 2 to 10 km of priority road affected
Major: over 10 km affected, or run abandoned

freeze_proximity.instructions: How soon will the earliest untreated priority road reach freezing?
criteria: No untreated priority road, or no freeze within 12 hours
Earliest untreated road freezes in 6 to 12 hours
Earliest untreated road freezes in 2 to 6 hours
Under 2 hours to freezing, or already frozen

factors.name: missed_extent
factors.description: Total length of priority road with no spreading recorded, or a logged rate below the approved rate, after closures and partner coverage are excluded

factors.name: missed_section_mitigated
factors.description: Whether an apparently untreated section is covered by a benign explanation: an approved road closure reference, or treatment logged by a second vehicle or a neighbouring authority under a mutual-aid agreement

factors.name: salt_gap
factors.description: Difference between net salt used (loaded minus returned) and the expected quantity (rate x treated length x width)

factors.name: rate_exception_approved
factors.description: Whether a reduced spread rate was authorised for this run, for example pre-wetted salt or residual salt from an earlier run. This changes the expected tonnage and can explain a low usage figure.

factors.name: finish_vs_freeze_min
factors.description: Minutes between the last priority section's treatment end time in telematics and that zone's forecast freeze time. Negative means treatment ended after the freeze time.

factors.name: hours_to_freeze_untreated
factors.description: Hours from log review time until the earliest untreated priority section's zone reaches 0°C under the latest forecast revision. Values cluster near the 2, 6 and 12 hour boundaries in some records.

factors.name: forecast_revised
factors.description: Whether a later forecast revision moved the freeze time. A warmer revision delays it and acts as mitigation; a colder revision brings it forward.

factors.name: crosscheck_mismatch
factors.description: Where a cross-section discrepancy sits, if anywhere. Some are trivial: registration spacing, or kg against tonnes with equal values. Others are material: a section code missing from telematics, or a log date differing from the telematics date.

factors.name: driver_note_type
factors.description: Content of the driver's free-text note

factors.name: follow_up_run_scheduled
factors.description: Whether a subsequent run covering the same route is already scheduled to finish before the forecast freeze time, which reduces the need for extra dispatch

factors.name: pending_confirmation
factors.description: Whether one key datum is awaiting confirmation, so that a single answer would settle the log. Examples: a weighbridge ticket number is null, or a partner authority's coverage is not yet confirmed.

factors.name: gps_dropouts
factors.description: Count of telematics signal dropouts during the run. Some overlap priority sections and leave coverage unproven; others fall on non-priority or transit stretches as decoys.

factors.name: nonpriority_untreated
factors.description: Whether some non-priority (secondary network) sections were left untreated. This is a decoy that does not count towards priority deficiency.

sections.name: run_header
sections.description: run_id, route_code, vehicle_reg, driver_id, run_date, decision_ref, run_type (precautionary/reactive), reviewed_at timestamp

sections.name: plan
sections.description: List of route sections: section_code, length_km, width_m, priority (P1/P2/secondary), planned_rate_gm2, forecast_zone

sections.name: forecast
sections.description: Per-zone rst_min_c and freeze_time, plus a revisions list with issued_at and the revised freeze_time per zone

sections.name: telematics
sections.description: List of treated segments (section_code, start, end, spread_on, logged_rate_gm2), a dropouts list with start, end and nearest_section, and the telematics vehicle_reg and date

sections.name: materials
sections.description: loaded_t, returned_t (null if unknown), weighbridge_ticket, rate_exception object (approved_by, reduced_rate_gm2, reason) or null

sections.name: notes
sections.description: driver_note and depot_note one-line free text, plus a closures list (section_code, closure_ref, authority) and partner_cover list

rendering_notes: missed_extent appears only indirectly. Plan sections with priority P1/P2 either have no matching telematics segment, have spread_on false, or have logged_rate_gm2 below the planned rate (or below reduced_rate_gm2 where a rate_exception exists). The reader must sum the lengths. When missed_section_mitigated is true, the missing section appears in notes.closures with a closure_ref, or in partner_cover with a vehicle or authority and times. Such a section is not counted as missed. salt_gap is never stated: the reader computes expected tonnes as rate × length_km × 1000 × width_m / 1e6 over the treated sections, and compares it with loaded_t minus returned_t. figure_missing sets returned_t or weighbridge_ticket to null. rate_exception_approved fills materials.rate_exception; otherwise it is null. Where it exists, a low usage figure becomes consistent, and it changes which rate counts as undertreated. finish_vs_freeze_min arises from the last P1/P2 telematics end time against forecast.freeze_time for that section's zone, using the latest revision. hours_to_freeze_untreated is derived from run_header.reviewed_at and the revised freeze_time of the zone holding the earliest untreated priority section. forecast_revised adds an entry to forecast.revisions; the original freeze_time remains visible as a decoy. crosscheck_mismatch places the discrepancy between run_header and telematics (vehicle_reg, date), between plan and telematics (section_code such as A417-06 against A417-6, or a code absent altogether), or in materials units (loaded given in kg in the depot_note against tonnes in materials). reg_format and unit_kg_t with equal values are trivial; section_code and date_mismatch are material. driver_note_type gives one sentence. alarming_resolved reads like 'Spinner jammed near Holt Lane, cleared after ten minutes and section re-run', with a matching second telematics segment. alarming_unresolved reads like 'Chute blocked from the roundabout onwards, returned to depot' with no further segments. Routine and blank notes carry no signal. follow_up_run_scheduled appears in the depot_note, for example 'Run R2 booked out 03:30 on same route', with no explicit link to the gap. pending_confirmation appears as a null weighbridge_ticket, or a partner_cover entry with confirmed: false. gps_dropouts are listed with nearest_section; only dropouts on priority sections with no other segment evidence leave coverage unproven. Untreated nonpriority sections carry the 'secondary' priority and are decoys. No field may state completion status, deficiency, urgency, reconciliation result or recommended action. There are no fields like 'status: incomplete', 'missed_km' or 'priority: urgent'; every answer must be derived by comparing sections.
